title: Second-order active-engine Top20 hit-count regime
hypothesis: Does the pair of prior active-engine Top20 hit counts (H[t-1], H[t-2]) add predictive information for H[t] beyond the exact Hypergeometric(40,20,5) null and the first-order state H[t-1]?
outcome_definition: H[t] is the number of winning numbers in the exact active-engine Top20 frozen before target t.

walk_forward.excluded_first_source_row: Lag-2 state unavailable for the first ledger row; its outcome is retained as prior M1 training data.
walk_forward.order: For target i, score before adding target i outcome; M1 uses all prior transitions; M2 uses prior transitions with an observed second lag.

limitations: Q114 is exploratory and was not preregistered before the initial historical computation; the protocol records this limitation.
Historical Blind OOS is not a virgin holdout and has been examined by related SONAR research.
The Top20 hit-count sequence is derived from the active engine and historical outcomes; it tests calibration of hit-count probabilities, not winning-number prediction.
The fixed alpha=200 is inherited from Q113; no alpha grid or subgroup tuning was performed.
Holm correction covers the two Q114 primary endpoints only, not the entire Q00-Q114 research family.
The prospective 2026-11-11 freeze is a single descriptive observation until the official result is available.
